s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic eye symptoms with progressive vision loss and conjunctival abnormalities
key_facts: Initial visual acuity was 20/20 OD and 20/30 OS
Vision deteriorated to 20/30 OD and counting fingers OS over time
Slit lamp examination revealed subconjunctival fibrosis
Slit lamp examination revealed symblepharon formation
Slit lamp examination revealed corneal neovascularizations
Slit lamp examination revealed conjunctival hyperemia
Conjunctival biopsy and immunofluorescent histology revealed an unspecific result
Reduction in conjunctival hyperemia and corneal vascularizations after therapy

shortlist.label: conjunctivitis
shortlist.why_kept: conjunctival hyperemia and response to therapy

raw.rationale: The presence of subconjunctival fibrosis, symblepharon formation, corneal neovascularizations, and conjunctival hyperemia, along with the deterioration of vision, are consistent with limbal stem cell deficiency, which can lead to chronic eye symptoms and vision loss due to the impairment of the corneal epithelium's ability to regenerate.

rejected.label: scleritis
rejected.why: Scleritis typically presents with severe eye pain and tenderness, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: conjunctivitis
rejected.why: Conjunctivitis usually presents with discharge and itching, which are not mentioned, and the symptoms described are more severe than typical conjunctivitis.

rejected.label: keratitis
rejected.why: Keratitis typically presents with corneal inflammation and pain, but the presence of symblepharon formation and subconjunctival fibrosis suggests a more complex condition.

rejected.label: uveitis
rejected.why: Uveitis typically presents with pain, redness, and sensitivity to light, and the symptoms described do not specifically point to uveitis, especially with the absence of mention of intraocular inflammation.
